title: 1st Abyss 1st Matter In Universal Questions Denial Is Worthless Against Proof

questions.question: What does this part say will be discussed in four questions?
questions.answer: Two dangers that make faith feel shaky and bring doubts.

questions.question: How many helpful points are given for being saved from the first danger?
questions.answer: Two.

questions.question: In general matters, what is weak when clear proof is present?
questions.answer: Denial.

questions.question: In the moon example, who gives the strong proof?
questions.answer: The two ordinary men who saw it.

questions.question: In that same example, what do the many others say?
questions.answer: They say they did not see it.

questions.question: Why does the sighting still count even if many people deny it?
questions.answer: Because seeing it is proof, but not seeing it is not strong proof.

questions.question: When people affirm something with proof, how do they help each other?
questions.answer: They support one another and become stronger together.

questions.question: When people deny something, do they join together in the same strong way?
questions.answer: No. Each one stays by himself.

questions.question: If one person says something exists, what may be enough to show it?
questions.answer: One clear sign.

questions.question: If someone says a thing does not exist anywhere, what very hard job would he need to do?
questions.answer: He would need to search everywhere very fully.

questions.question: Why can deniers not really back each other up?
questions.answer: Because each one judges from his own limited seeing and understanding.

questions.question: What can a person honestly say if he has not seen something?
questions.answer: He can say he does not see it.

questions.question: What should he not claim as a fact?
questions.answer: He should not claim that it truly does not exist at all.

questions.question: In belief matters, how serious is it to say something does not exist everywhere?
questions.answer: It is a huge false claim.

questions.question: What does this passage focus on instead of giving the full long explanation?
questions.answer: It gives only two deep dangers that trouble faith in this time.

questions.question: What is the title of the first helpful point for the first danger?
questions.answer: The First Matter.

questions.question: In broad questions, which is stronger: proving or denying?
questions.answer: Proving is stronger.

questions.question: What example is used to show this?
questions.answer: Looking for the new Ramadan moon.

questions.question: If two people see the moon, what do they bring?
questions.answer: Witness and proof.

questions.question: If many respected people say they did not see it, what is missing from their words?
questions.answer: Strong proof.

questions.question: Why do people who prove something become stronger together?
questions.answer: Because they point to the same real thing.

questions.question: Why do people who deny something stay separate?
questions.answer: Because each one speaks only from his own view.

questions.question: What simple action in the example shows two people uniting on one truth?
questions.answer: One points it out and the other sees the same thing.

questions.question: Is it easy to show that something exists?
questions.answer: Yes, one sign can be enough.

questions.question: Is it easy to show that something never exists anywhere?
questions.answer: No, that would be extremely hard.

questions.question: What makes deniers judge wrongly?
questions.answer: Their own limits, veils, and blocked sight.

questions.question: Which sentence is careful and honest: “I do not see it” or “It is not real at all”?
questions.answer: “I do not see it.”

questions.question: Why is the second sentence dangerous in matters of faith?
questions.answer: Because it claims too much without full knowledge.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the number of people against belief?
questions.answer: Big numbers do not give real strength to denial.

questions.question: How many deep dangers are mentioned at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: Two.

questions.question: What is the first rescue step about?
questions.answer: It explains why denial is weak against proof.

questions.question: In the example, what event in the sky is being talked about?
questions.answer: The first thin moon of Ramadan.

questions.question: Do the two witnesses have to be famous people for their proof to count?
questions.answer: No. Even ordinary people can give valid witness.

questions.question: Why are the many people who did not see it not enough to defeat the proof?
questions.answer: Because not seeing something is not the same as proving it is absent.

questions.question: What happens when several people affirm one true thing?
questions.answer: Their statements support one another.

questions.question: What happens when several people deny from personal limits?
questions.answer: Their statements stay separate.

questions.question: Why can one sign establish that something is real?
questions.answer: Because the thing only needs to be shown in one true place.

questions.question: Why is denying existence everywhere much harder?
questions.answer: Because a person would need complete search and knowledge.

questions.question: What does the passage say about someone who judges only by himself?
questions.answer: He cannot give strong support to others who also deny.

questions.question: What is a person allowed to say about his own sight?
questions.answer: He can say he did not notice it.

questions.question: What can he not truthfully say about all reality?
questions.answer: He cannot truthfully say it is nowhere at all.

questions.question: In belief questions, how big is such a false claim?
questions.answer: As big as the whole world.

questions.question: What kind of questions does the passage say it will use as a frame?
questions.answer: Four questions.

questions.question: What are these questions meant to address?
questions.answer: Two deep causes of doubt in faith today.

questions.question: What is the first matter mainly teaching?
questions.answer: That proof is strong and denial is weak.

questions.question: Which month’s moon is used as the example?
questions.answer: Ramadan.

questions.question: If two people truly see the moon, what do they have?
questions.answer: A real witness.

questions.question: If many people say only that they missed seeing it, what do they not have?
questions.answer: They do not have proof that it is absent.

questions.question: Why does affirmation lead to unity?
questions.answer: Because people are confirming the same thing.

questions.question: Why does negation not lead to the same unity?
questions.answer: Because each denial comes from a separate person’s limits.

questions.question: To prove something exists, how much evidence may be needed?
questions.answer: Even one clear clue may be enough.

questions.question: To prove something never existed anywhere, how much would someone need to know?
questions.answer: He would need to know everything everywhere and through time.

questions.question: What blocks deniers from true judgment?
questions.answer: Their own veils and causes of not seeing.

questions.question: What personal statement may someone make without lying?
questions.answer: That he himself does not see it.

questions.question: What universal statement should he not make?
questions.answer: That the thing is truly not there at all.

questions.question: What does the passage say has already been proven strongly elsewhere?
questions.answer: This truth about faith.

questions.question: So what does this part choose to explain briefly?
questions.answer: Two dangers that shake certainty.

questions.question: What is the first thing taught for rescue from the first danger?
questions.answer: Denial cannot stand strong against proof.

questions.question: What example helps explain this?
questions.answer: The beginning moon of Ramadan.

questions.question: If a few people truly see the moon, what kind of evidence is that?
questions.answer: Positive evidence.

questions.question: If many others just say they did not see it, why is that not equal?
questions.answer: Because their words do not prove the moon was not there.

questions.question: How do people who affirm a fact work together?
questions.answer: They strengthen one another.

questions.question: How do people who deny a fact stand?
questions.answer: Each one stands alone.

questions.question: What is easier: showing something exists or proving it exists nowhere?
questions.answer: Showing it exists.

questions.question: Why is proving nonexistence everywhere so hard?
questions.answer: Because it needs a full search of all places and even times.

questions.question: What do deniers often use to judge?
questions.answer: Their own small view and understanding.

questions.question: What is the safe limit of their claim?
questions.answer: They can only speak about what they did not see.

questions.question: Why is a sweeping denial in belief matters called a huge lie?
questions.answer: Because no person has that much complete knowledge.

questions.question: What should believers remember when many people oppose faith?
questions.answer: Many deniers together still do not make denial strong.

questions.question: What kind of certainty is said to be shaken in this age?
questions.answer: Certainty of faith.

questions.question: How many matters are given as help for the first danger?
questions.answer: Two matters.

questions.question: What does the first matter compare: proof or denial?
questions.answer: It compares their strength and shows proof is stronger.

questions.question: What religious sign is used as the example?
questions.answer: The new moon for Ramadan.

questions.question: What makes the report of the two men strong?
questions.answer: They actually saw it.

questions.question: Why do the many others not defeat that report?
questions.answer: Because they only speak from not seeing it themselves.

questions.question: What happens when people confirm one real thing together?
questions.answer: Their witness joins and becomes stronger.

questions.question: What happens when people deny from separate limits?
questions.answer: Their denial does not unite in the same way.

questions.question: If you want to show that something is real, what may be enough?
questions.answer: One clear sign or indication.

questions.question: If you want to show that something is nowhere at all, what would you need?
questions.answer: A complete search everywhere.

questions.question: Why are deniers unable to support each other well?
questions.answer: Because each one is blocked in a different way.

questions.question: What may a person say about his own experience?
questions.answer: He may say he did not see it.

questions.question: What may he not say about reality as a whole?
questions.answer: He may not say it truly does not exist.

questions.question: In faith matters, how wrong is such a claim?
questions.answer: Very wrong and very huge.

questions.question: What should we think about the large crowd of deniers?
questions.answer: Their number does not give real proof.
